CDCLocator working guidance

Source: AGENTS.md

Adapted from CDCAtlas’s AGENTS.md at fef315a. Do not regenerate this file from a template; review changes against the committed version.

Scope and authority

This file applies to all substantive CDCLocator work: implementation, design, debugging, tests, documentation and review. Read REVIEWING.md for shared review standards. Neither repository files nor skills expand the user’s permissions; direct user instructions control.

Repository: https://github.com/VagishHemmige/CDCLocator The default branch was verified as master on 2026-11-15; verify it again when selecting a base. This guidance does not cover CDCAtlas or other repos.

Use available project conversations to understand intent. Automated runs may not receive every conversation or uploaded file. State material context gaps. Record agreed technical decisions and rationale in issues, linking them from PRs and relevant documentation. Preserve the durable technical decision without copying private conversations. Distinguish accepted decisions from proposals in issue discussions.

Architecture

CDCLocator is a development-stage R client for the HIV.gov Locator API (https://locator-api.hiv.gov). It finds HIV and related service providers near a ZIP code, city and state, or point, and returns tibbles.

  • R/request.R: .cdc_locator_request() builds every request (base URL, auth headers, query, timeout) and .perform_cdc_locator_request() performs it, checks the status and parses JSON. All API calls go through these two helpers.
  • R/auth.R: .build_auth_headers() finds credentials (arguments first, then the CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_ID and CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_TOKEN environment variables); cdc_locator_set_credentials() helps the user add them to .Renviron.
  • R/providers.R: cdc_providers(), providers within a radius of a ZIP code.
  • R/providers_tidy.R: cdc_providers_tidy(), flattens the nested provider columns returned by cdc_providers().
  • R/address_place.R, R/address_point.R: cdc_address_place() and cdc_address_point(), translate a city and state or a latitude and longitude into a ZIP code.
  • R/enums.R: the valid services values and their validator.
  • R/utils.R: small internal helpers, including the argument checks.
  • vignettes/: the user guide: getting started, credentials and networks, services and searching, working with results, and troubleshooting. Their code runs only when built with credentials and CDC_LOCATOR_LIVE_TESTS=true. Update them, and README.Rmd, when behavior or error messages change.

Read the relevant source and documentation before advising on or changing it. Offline tests mock every request; tests/testthat/test-live.R holds the live checks. GitHub Actions runs R CMD check, documentation and coverage checks on each PR, and the live tests only on request (live-tests.yaml).

The API’s 2025 access instructions are not public and are partly out of date. Behavior observed on 2026-11-16 that the code relies on:

  • /providers requires both radius and services; leaving either out gives HTTP 500 with a plain-text message.
  • Service values are lowercase (hepc, not the documented Hepc).
  • Services combine as “any of”: a request with two or three services returned the union of their single-service results. All 14 in one request returned no providers, so cdc_providers() sends at most three per request.
  • Validation errors are HTTP 500 with a plain-text body; a rejected token is HTTP 403 with a JSON Message.
  • Requests from outside the US got HTTP 403 from CloudFront (an HTML page). On 2026-11-16, GitHub-hosted runners on AWS us-east-1 reached the API and runners on Azure (eastus2, centralus) got 403 on every request, while the same key worked from the maintainer’s home connection on 2026-11-17. This is one day’s observation, not a guarantee from the provider.
  • A 403 can also mean a wrong or inactive key, so a 403 in a live run is not evidence of either cause by itself. Before assigning a cause, check the runner’s cloud and region in the job log and the sanitized error text, and repeat the same request at the same revision from a network known to work (usually the maintainer’s machine).

Recheck these against the live API when request or parsing code changes.

Implementation and approval

A review or explanation request alone does not authorize implementation. For requested changes, draft and self-review in an isolated workspace. The user’s connected working copy and active RStudio session remain read-only: no execution there.

Before commitment, obtain the user’s approval for each behavior-changing file, including arguments, outputs, request parameters, error conditions and how missing or empty responses are returned. Finish the concrete draft and appropriate checks first. Show a readable diff for every changed file: side-by-side when supported, otherwise unified. Show complete new files and provide access to complete changed files. Explain what changed, why, behavior changes and validation actually performed. Separate human-written and mechanical generated changes. Request approval for the specific files and revision shown; a summary alone is insufficient.

When two or more alternatives are reasonable, present them with their tradeoffs and a recommendation before settling the design. Consider a function argument with a recommended default when alternatives serve plausible user needs; an argument is a proposal, not an automatic requirement. Seek the maintainer’s decision before implementation.

What each assistant may commit, push, post, merge or delete is set by the maintainer outside this repository. This file grants none of those permissions. Inspect mechanical generated changes before including them with approved source; material behavior changes after approval require renewed approval. Self-review is not independent review. Identify assistant authorship in the PR body so independent review can be routed correctly.

Credentials and execution boundaries

The API needs a client ID and a client token. Treat both as secrets.

  • Never ask for, read, print, copy or commit real credentials, including from .Renviron, .env, environment variables or shell history.
  • Offline tests and examples use obviously fake values, for example withr::local_envvar(CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_ID = "fake-id", CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_TOKEN = "fake-token").
  • If a real-looking credential appears in code, tests, fixtures or git history, report its location without repeating its value.
  • Package code must not show credentials in errors, messages, printed requests or verbose output. Auth headers should be redacted in httr2 requests.
  • Recorded responses are made on the maintainer’s machine. Before one is committed, check it for credentials and auth headers and say what was checked.
  • CI reads credentials only from the CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_ID and CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_TOKEN repository secrets, with ${{ secrets.NAME }}. Never print, log or commit their values.

Inspect startup files, helpers, test configuration and package load-time behavior before execution; do not load secrets or copy private startup settings. Use clean sessions and isolated temporary locations. New package code writes only to tempdir() unless the caller explicitly supplies a destination. Adding caching or any persistent file location requires approval.

Run devtools::document() only in isolation when relevant; exclude unrelated Rd and incidental DESCRIPTION/RoxygenNote churn. Format R code with Air (air format) on the files a change touches and only those; don’t reformat other files, and don’t use styler. Inspect generated exports and imports rather than assuming they are safe.

Skills and validation

Use applicable R package-development and critical-code-review guidance for substantive work. Add testing and test-review guidance for tests or untested behavior, cli guidance for conditions, CRAN guidance for DESCRIPTION, examples, vignettes or CRAN preparation, and lifecycle guidance for deprecations. Names vary by environment: r-testthat / testing-r-packages, r-cli / cli, r-cran-extrachecks / cran-extrachecks, and r-lifecycle / lifecycle. Use the installed equivalent. Disclose unavailable skills. Permission boundaries and this project’s formatting rule (Air, touched files only) take precedence over skill defaults.

Prefer regression tests demonstrating the bug before the fix. Keep routine tests reproducible and independent of the live API: mock at the package’s own request boundary or with httr2::local_mocked_responses(). Mocks establish code behavior, not current API compatibility.

Live tests are gated by CDC_LOCATOR_LIVE_TESTS=true and also need both credential variables; without them they skip. Keep live requests few and small. Run them when request building, response parsing or tidying changes. Report actual runtime and network availability rather than assuming either.

Integrate useful review-created checks into the existing owning test files with the corresponding approved fix. Do not install known failures, expected-failure assertions or unjustified skips as standing CI.

Separate source inspection, personally executed offline checks, recorded responses, live API checks, observed CI and author-reported validation. Record live retrieval dates and tested requests without credentials. Supply exact commands for remaining maintainer checks, with prerequisites and side effects.

Automation triggers, comment permissions, deduplication and notifications belong in automation configuration. This file does not start automation or grant publishing authority.

Package conventions

  • Use US English and sentence-case headings. Follow existing tidyverse style, using the base pipe and single-line anonymous-function shorthand where appropriate. Do not perform unrelated style cleanup.
  • Put tests for R/{name}.R in tests/testthat/test-{name}.R. Keep test code inside test_that(); shared setup belongs in helpers. For errors and warnings, prefer snapshots when message text matters; use class-based expectations when testing a known condition class.
  • Document and export public functions with roxygen2. Internal helpers should not create public help topics; use @noRd. Wrap roxygen comments to 80 characters. Add new public topics to _pkgdown.yml and check reference coverage with pkgdown::check_pkgdown().
  • Give user-facing changes a NEWS.md bullet, except small documentation changes, internal refactoring and fixes to the current development version. Put the function name early and the related issue in parentheses. Keep each bullet on one line, order function bullets alphabetically, and put non-function bullets first.
  • When committing is authorized, use Markdown in the commit message without wrapping its lines; include Fixes #num. on its own line when applicable.

Documentation maintenance

For a commissioned whole-package review, follow PACKAGE_REVIEW.md.

The paths above describe the current layout. Update them when files move. .Rbuildignore excludes AGENTS.md, REVIEWING.md and PACKAGE_REVIEW.md from package builds, not from pkgdown, so they can become unlinked website pages. Do not claim these files are unpublished or private.
